newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU agrees aid for Albania.
newsitem.headline: EU agrees aid for Albania.

text.p: The European Commission said on Wednesday it had agreed to send two million Ecus ($2.3 million) worth of humanitarian aid to help victims of the crisis in Albania.

The aid, managed by the EU's humanitarian office ECHO, will enable the International Committee of the Red Cross to distribute food and medical supplies for about 10,000 people, the Commission said in a statement.
"The lawlessness which has gripped the country over the past few weeks has exposed some Albanians to extreme hardship," it said.
A European Union mission to Albania had identified the most vulnerable people as those living in state institutions like hospitals, orphanages, and homes for old people and the handicapped.

An advance team of European experts left Rome for Tirana on Wednesday to assess the scale of a planned multinational relief operation in Albania which has been swept by violence since January when a series of popular but fraudulent investment schemes collapsed, wiping out millions of dollars in savings.
Riots and protests against the schemes were followed by a popular uprising in the south with thousands of people seizing weapons from army depots and setting up rebel councils.

The European Commission statement said it would be monitoring the situation closely with a view to guaranteeing that adequate protection is provided for both goods and people involved with the relief effort.
It is being extra vigilant after an incident in Vlore in which Italian medical staff were held hostage by unidentified rebels.
